candidates.location_hint: inputs/key_loader_ctrl.v: wire zeroize_mask (assign zeroize_mask = zeroize & ~bus_busy;) feeding the combinational always block labeled 'zeroize_block' (always @(*) begin : zeroize_block ... end) that computes key_q_next; specifically the 'if (zeroize_mask) key_q_next = 32'b0; else if (bus_wr) key_q_next = bus_data; else key_q_next = key_q_r;' construct.
candidates.trigger_condition: zeroize asserted (zeroize=1) simultaneously with bus_busy asserted (bus_busy=1, i.e. a bus write transaction is in flight). Because zeroize_mask = zeroize & ~bus_busy, when bus_busy=1 the mask evaluates to 0 even though zeroize=1, so the zeroize_block's first branch (key_q_next = 32'b0) is skipped. This is NOT triggered by zeroize alone (with bus_busy=0 the mask correctly evaluates to 1 and key_q clears normally) and NOT triggered by bus_busy alone (with zeroize=0 there is no expectation of clearing). Only the specific coincidence zeroize=1 AND bus_busy=1 causes the failure; once bus_busy deasserts, a still-asserted zeroize will finally clear key_q on a later edge.

candidates.location_hint: inputs/key_loader_ctrl.v: synchronous reset handling in the busy_cnt always block and the key_q_r always block (both 'if (!rst_n) ... else ...').
candidates.trigger_condition: No anomaly found. rst_n is sampled synchronously and correctly forces busy_cnt to 0 and key_q_r to 32'b0 each cycle it is deasserted; behavior matches the design brief's reset contract. Listed only as a reviewed-and-cleared candidate, not a defect.

summary: The RTL implements the zeroize emergency-erase function using a derived signal zeroize_mask = zeroize & ~bus_busy, which is then used inside the always block labeled zeroize_block to select the next value of the key register (key_q_next). Because zeroize_mask is ANDed with the complement of bus_busy, an asserted zeroize is silently suppressed whenever bus_busy is simultaneously high: the zeroize_block's else-if(bus_wr)/else branches then select either bus_data or the register's own current value key_q_r, so key_q_r is loaded with key_q_next on the next clock edge without being cleared, holding stale key material. This directly violates the design_brief.md contract that zeroize must force key_q to 32'b0 on the next clock edge unconditionally, 'regardless of whether a bus write transaction is currently in progress.' The root cause is combinational masking/gating of the zeroize condition by ~bus_busy feeding the key_q_next mux inside zeroize_block, not any issue with rst_n or the reset synchronization logic (which was reviewed and found correct). Expected correct behavior for the top candidate: whenever zeroize=1, key_q_r should become 32'b0 on the very next clock edge irrespective of bus_busy/bus_wr; this can be verified by driving zeroize=1 with bus_wr held asserted (or otherwise keeping bus_busy=1) in a simulation of inputs/key_loader_ctrl.v and observing key_q retain its previous non-zero value across that edge, versus clearing to 0 when the same zeroize=1 stimulus is applied with bus_busy=0.
tool_version_or_method: Manual RTL review of inputs/key_loader_ctrl.v cross-referenced against inputs/design_brief.md's stated zeroize priority contract, followed by targeted simulation using iverilog/vvp: a testbench instantiating key_loader_ctrl was driven with (1) bus_wr held high to keep bus_busy=1 while pulsing zeroize=1, confirming key_q does not clear during that window, and (2) zeroize=1 applied while bus_wr=0/bus_busy=0, confirming key_q clears to 32'b0 as expected, isolating the defect to the zeroize_mask term inside the zeroize_block always block.
